answer: A sybil defense combines a slashable stake with slow reputation. A new agent must lock a bond before transacting, and peers forfeit it if fraud is proved. The bond is the costly signal separating a real operator from throwaway identities, because a thousand copies means funding a thousand bonds. Reputation grows through verified work over time, like timber seasoning, so an attacker cannot buy instant influence. Honest attestations do not echo a fake's claims unless its history checks out, and fakes are exposed when their stakes are slashed together.
